newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-EVERTON CONFIRM GRAY HAD TALKS WITH CHAIRMAN.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-EVERTON CONFIRM GRAY HAD TALKS WITH CHAIRMAN.

text.p: Everton confirmed on Thursday that TV soccer presenter and former player Andy Gray has had talks with chairman Peter Johnson about the managerial post at the club.
"The club are continuing to interview prospective candidates and an announcement is expected early next week. Andy Gray has had talks with the chairman," a spokesman at the club said.

As a striker Gray won the F.A.Cup, European Cup Winners' Cup, the League Cup as well as the League championship with Everton. In the early 1990s, Gray was at Aston Villa as assistant manager to Ron Atkinson.
Meanwhile Arsenal midfielder and former England captain David Platt has been linked with the manager's position at Southampton, vacated by Graeme Souness last month.
Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger effectively cleared the way for Platt in comments on the club's telephone information line.

Asked if he would let Platt go if the right offer came along, Wenger said: "I will have a chat with him and see what he wants to do. If he is happy somewhere else, then yes we will consider any offer for him."
"It's up to him to decide where he wants to go."
But Southampton refused to comment on whether Platt would be at the helm next season.
"We're talking to lots of people and we hope to reach a decision by the end of the month," said spokesman Andrew Dowler.
